budget_items.what_was_said: The commission reviewed the sale-of-lots fund balance after the $10,000 transfer into the capital article fund that town meeting approved the night before.
The prior capital article balance was combined with the new transfer, ahead of adding the capital plan budget for the back lot.
The chair read the perpetual care fund's expendable balance carried from a previous report.
Stone wall repair in South Cemetery and hedge plantings/trimming were confirmed as already invoiced against perpetual care.
After invoiced work, the commission worked out roughly how much remained in perpetual care, reading the figure haltingly.
The commission noted approved funding for the Fish Street wall and set aside a remainder for South cemetery work, leaving only a small balance.

decisions.decision: Fold into the minutes approval a decision to send a letter to the Select Board requesting an additional person to work with DPW at the cemetery.
Install temporary solar lights atop the flagpoles rather than pursue a permanent in-ground lighting system, funded from perpetual care.
Hold off ordering the second Goodrich plaque and additional stone repair/power-washing work until spring.
Ask the town/finance director for a regular (monthly or quarterly) report on perpetual care and sale-of-lots fund activity.
Adopt a new sign-off procedure where the superintendent and a commissioner sign a simple account/amount form at the meeting, to avoid missing town payment cutoffs.
Postpone the South Cemetery headstone straightening and repair project until spring due to expected ground frost.
Set the next meeting for December 11th.
Cemeteries remain open until ice/snow conditions require closure, and will reopen once conditions improve.

minutes.summary: The Cemetery Commission approved its October minutes along with a request to the Select Board for an additional DPW staff person, reviewed how a $10,000 town-meeting warrant transfer and perpetual care funds are being spent on the Fish Street wall, flagpole lighting and the Captain Levi Goodrich memorial plaque, and adopted a new sign-off procedure with the town to keep contractor payments from missing cutoffs. Several stone-wall and headstone repair projects in South Cemetery were pushed to spring, and the board asked the town for regular reporting on fund balances going forward.

what_happened.line: The Commission voted to send the Select Board a letter requesting an additional DPW staff position for the cemetery.
A new sign-off procedure was adopted, requiring the superintendent and a commissioner to sign account forms at the meeting to avoid missing town payment cutoffs.
Flagpole lighting will use temporary solar fixtures instead of a permanent in-ground system, paid from perpetual care funds.
South Cemetery stone wall and headstone repair work was pushed to spring because of expected ground frost.
The Commission asked the town for regular reporting on perpetual care and sale-of-lots fund balances.

why_it_matters: A staffing request to the Select Board could add a budgeted position, which residents may see reflected in a future town budget vote.
Cemetery repairs and improvements described here are funded from perpetual care and sale-of-lots trust funds, not directly from the tax levy.
The new payment sign-off procedure is a process change meant to keep contractor invoices from missing town cutoffs, not a new expense.
